section_summary: This section continues a report on Japan’s naval construction program and then records Japanese notifications of vessel keel layings and completions under Article 10 of the London Naval Treaty, with State Department acknowledgments and copies forwarded to the Navy Department. It also contains correspondence about suspected military use of Japanese freighters, concern over Japanese naval expansion, a supplier’s request for advice about Japanese Navy payments, and two document file notes.

subfiles.title: Report on Japan’s naval construction program
subfiles.about: Discusses Diet debate over Japan’s naval strength and construction plans under the naval treaties.
subfiles.summary: The report recounts Admiral Abe’s answers about cruiser ratios, heavy cruiser construction time, and the risks of a failed future naval conference. It outlines a construction program of cruisers, destroyers, submarines, a mine-layer, smaller craft, and aircraft, while explaining why Japan deferred some treaty-allowed vessels.

subfiles.title: Confidential letter on Japanese naval expansion
subfiles.to: Secretary to the President of the United States
subfiles.about: Warns that Japan’s naval growth could threaten U.S. security.
subfiles.summary: The writer argues that Japan may seek control in Manchuria and China and eventually threaten U.S. possessions and shipping. He urges close attention to Japan’s international position and discusses the financial and political obstacles to building more American ships.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese Navy payment risk
subfiles.about: Requests advice on the credit risk of selling goods to the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: Cites delayed payments, a $13,000 invoice, and a pending $26,000 order.

subfiles.title: Reply to National Carbon Company
subfiles.about: Declines to assess the risk of Japanese Navy orders.
subfiles.summary: States that the Department offers no such opinions and has no nonpublic information.

subfiles.summary: References a conversation with Joyner about four submarines.
